content.text: {"headline":"No action needed: both queues are predicted at 100% service level for 15:30-17:30, above the 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"General has had 4-6 fewer agents than planned since 15:00 (23-24 on the phones against 28-29 planned), and calls are running 16% above forecast (1712 vs 1476). Even so, the forecast shows payments and general both at 100% service level with 0% abandons through the disruption window, and 98.2% for the rest of the day. The cause of the missing agents is still unknown. Absence doesn't explain it: there has been 1 sick call against a usual 1.9. It may be a planned shift start that didn't happen.","trade_offs":["The free callback options (P2 on general 15:30-17:30, P3 on both queues 18:00-20:00) predict exactly the same results as doing nothing, so they add complexity without any forecast benefit.","Doing nothing carries no cost and no risk to payments, but there is no safety net if the missing agents stay off or calls keep rising beyond today's 16% uplift."],"watch":"Check with the team leads or WFM whether the 15:00 shift start on general was missed, and track whether agents on the phones recover to 28-29. If general's service level starts to slip or call volume climbs further, P2's free callback on general is a ready fallback."}
